questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG from a patient with sharp chest pain that improves on sitting up and leaning forward demonstrates the labeled changes across multiple leads. What is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Diffuse ST-segment elevation with PR-segment depression across multiple leads (rather than a single vascular territory) is the classic ECG signature of acute pericarditis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diffuse ST-segment elevation with PR-segment depression across multiple leads (rather than a single vascular territory) is the classic ECG signature of acute pericarditis.

questions.stem: This gross valve specimen shows sterile vegetations distributed along the free margins of the leaflet in a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus. What eponymous term is used for this pattern of endocarditis?

explanation.summary: The sterile vegetations of SLE that form along leaflet margins (and can occur on both surfaces of the valve) are termed Libman-Sacks endocarditis, a form of NBTE.
explanation.whyCorrect: The sterile vegetations of SLE that form along leaflet margins (and can occur on both surfaces of the valve) are termed Libman-Sacks endocarditis, a form of NBTE.

questions.stem: This gross specimen shows a heart whose pericardial surface is coated with a thick, opaque, grossly purulent exudate. What organism is the most common cause of this condition?

explanation.summary: Purulent (bacterial) pericarditis produces grossly purulent pericardial fluid and is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Purulent (bacterial) pericarditis produces grossly purulent pericardial fluid and is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus.

questions.stem: This gross image shows a heart valve leaflet studded with small growths along its margin, with the underlying chordae visible. Which underlying condition most characteristically produces these lesions?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A hypercoagulable state such as malignancy or SLE

explanation.summary: The sterile platelet-fibrin vegetations shown form on the valve cusp margins in nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis, which arises from hypercoagulable states such as advanced malignancy, SLE (Libman-Sacks), or antiphospholipid syndrome rather than from infection or inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The sterile platelet-fibrin vegetations shown form on the valve cusp margins in nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis, which arises from hypercoagulable states such as advanced malignancy, SLE (Libman-Sacks), or antiphospholipid syndrome rather than from infection or inflammation.
